breaks.title: Legacy privacy-center revoke bypassed the consent ledger
breaks.detail: PUT /v1/me/ml-training-consent {granted:false} updated only the legacy ml_training_consent table and never appended a withdrawal to consent_record. The training gate (services/media-worker/src/trainingConsent.ts) reads only consent_record, so a user who granted via the ledger and revoked via the privacy center remained training-consented: any ml_dataset_item added AFTER the revoke was training-eligible. Demonstrated: RT-1 in services/api/test/consent.redteam.integration.test.ts fails with the fix reverted (gate still says consented after revoke).
breaks.fix: Privacy route revoke now appends a model_training 'withdrawn' consent_record (source privacy_center) in the same transaction. Grants are intentionally NOT mirrored: a ledger grant only ever comes from the explicit consent endpoint (default-deny direction preserved).

breaks.title: Status derivation ordered by millisecond-truncated timestamp, not ledger seq
breaks.detail: deriveConsentStatus sorted records by recordedAtIso (Date.toISOString truncates to ms). A withdraw recorded in the same millisecond as a grant, handed over in adversarial array order, derived active=true after withdrawal. Demonstrated: first test in packages/shared-types/test/consent.redteam.test.ts failed (active=true) before the fix. The API route was partially shielded (ORDER BY seq + stable sort) but the shared contract function was not.
breaks.fix: ConsentRecord gains optional seq (DB identity); deriveConsentStatus orders by seq when present, timestamp fallback for legacy payloads. API responses now expose seq (additive contract change; ConsentRecordSchema seq optional).

breaks.title: Withdrawal race with in-flight training-eligibility selection (TOCTOU)
breaks.status: FIXED (hardened; snapshot race is inherent, mitigated by mandatory re-verification)
breaks.detail: selectTrainingEligibleItems taken inside a transaction snapshot opened before a withdrawal commits still returns the withdrawn user's items; nothing forced consumers to re-check before training use. Demonstrated live against PostgreSQL: RT-7 in services/media-worker/test/trainingConsent.redteam.test.ts opens a REPEATABLE READ snapshot, commits a withdrawal on another connection, and the stale snapshot still selects the item.
breaks.fix: Added verifyTrainingEligibility(pool, items) — fresh-connection recheck that drops items whose users' latest ledger action is no longer 'granted' — plus selectTrainingEligibleItemsWithWatermark exposing the max consent_record.seq at selection time so consumers can detect stale selections. RT-7 proves the recheck excludes the withdrawn user's items.

breaks.title: Grant consent version invisible to training consumers across mid-session version upgrades
breaks.detail: TrainingEligibleItem exposed only ml_dataset_item.consent_version (stamped at ingest), not the version of the ledger grant currently authorizing the item. After a mid-session upgrade (re-grant under model-training-v2) consumers could not tell which contract version authorizes use.
breaks.fix: Selection now also returns grant_consent_version from the seq-latest ledger grant. No filtering was added by default (no blanket abstention): eligible-item coverage for existing v1 grants is unchanged — RT-9 and the pre-existing trainingConsent tests (12/12 green) confirm identical eligibility counts.

probed_no_break.title: Duplicate grants
probed_no_break.result: PASS — duplicates append (ledger is append-only by design), derived status stays consistent, every row audited (3 grants -> 3 audit_log rows).

probed_no_break.title: Withdraw-then-regrant audit trail
probed_no_break.result: PASS — trail granted->withdrawn->granted preserved; regrant does NOT resurrect ml_dataset_item rows flagged for removal review.

probed_no_break.title: Missing consent record treated as consent
probed_no_break.result: PASS — default deny holds everywhere probed: empty ledger, consent_subject row with zero model_training records, and the media-worker gate (absence never opt-in).

probed_no_break.title: Concurrent grant/withdraw
probed_no_break.result: PASS — concurrent requests append monotonically increasing seq; derived status matches the seq-latest record; DB append-only trigger intact.

open.title: Legacy privacy-center GRANT does not reach the ledger (fail-safe divergence)
open.detail: PUT /v1/me/ml-training-consent {granted:true} still writes only the legacy tables; the ledger gate continues to deny. This is the fail-safe direction (user believes they opted in but no training use happens). Unifying grant surfaces needs a product decision on which endpoint owns model_training opt-in; mirroring grants automatically would contradict the consent module's explicit-opt-in contract.

coverage_note: No abstention-based fixes: no eligibility was removed for validly consented users. Pre-existing gate tests (services/media-worker, 12/12) and consent ledger tests (services/api consent.integration, 8/8) green after fixes.
test_note: services/api test/training.integration.test.ts 'derives streaks...' fails identically on the unmodified base branch (training.completion_in_future — date-dependent, unrelated subsystem, untouched).
synthetic_fixtures: All red-team fixtures are synthetic and labeled as such in the test files; no held-out cases touched.
contracts: usable-result-v1 / silent-failure-v1 untouched. Consent contract change is additive only (optional seq field on ConsentRecord).
